text: This is a Choose Your Own Adventure (CYOA) style rich task.
You will be presented with a scenario and a series of choices.
Your goal is to navigate through the scenario by making decisions that will lead you to a successful outcome. Pay attention to the information provided, as it may help you make informed choices.
Generally speaking, commands will be enclosed in square brackets, e.g., [command]. After reading the context, type out your desired command and press enter.
You don't need to worry about capitalizing your commands.
You can also type [help] to see a list of available commands at any time.

content: You awaken on the space station Outer-11 and sign onto your terminal.
Your job as a diagnostic engineer is a slow one most days - thanks to the automated system that runs all operations.
You have one email.
Would you like to check your [email] or goof off and play [games] on you terminal?

response: - [GAMES]         :Goof off and play games on your terminal.

content: Your branch manager has sent you an email:
'Hey bud!
I got a ping this morning that there's some kind of energy issue.
Can you run a quick diagnostic?
Thanks pal!'
Would you like to run a system-wide [diagnostic] or ignore the email and [play] games on your terminal?

response: - [PLAY]          :Ignore the email and play games on your terminal.

content: You decide to ignore the email and play games on your terminal.
{CHECKED_EMAIL_TEXT}
You have an awesome time player Numbr Crunchrz 3000. You almost beat level 1.
You check your system clock, and realize that it has been 6 hours since you received the email.
Would you like to {CHECKED_EMAIL_OPTION} or keep playing [games] on your terminal?

text: Running the diagnostic would have been a waste of time anyways.

content: You run a diagnostic on the system. Your aging terminal spins up it's fans, wheezing dusty air.
You find that the engines, life support, escape pods, air locks, and docking bays are all operating as expected.
There is a problem. The Solar Generators are reporting many corrupted logs.
Would you like to send an [email] to your branch manager about the issue (it's been a hard day of work), or look into the [logs] yourself?

response: - [EMAIL]         :Send an email to your branch manager about the issue.

content: You successfully interpolate the missing data.
Looks like the solar batteries for the station are completely drained.
Luckily, the engines, docking bays, and auxiliary systems all have their own batteries, but they're draining fast.
Oddly enough - the Life Support systems are the only ones whose power level is rising...
Would you like to call it a day, sit back, and relax with some a [game] on your terminal, or [calculate] how long the station can survive on the remainining power?

response: - [GAME]          :Sit back and relax with a game on your terminal.
- [CALCULATE]     :Calculate how long the station can survive on the remaining power.

content: You abort the diagnostic and return to your terminal.
The solar generator logs are corrupted beyond repair - you have no idea what is going on there.
Would you like to [submit] the proper paperwork and escalate the issue to someone else, or try the [diagnostic] again?

response: - [SUBMIT]        :Submit the proper paperwork and escalate the issue to someone else.

content: You submit the proper forms detailing your failure to the branch manager.
You are promptly assured that the issue is likely nothing serious.
You are instructed to take a break and relax for the rest of your shift.
Life is good. [Continue]
You relax, and enjoy the rest of your shift playing Numbr Crunchrz 3000.
The day passes without incident. As does the next day.
By the end of the week, you notice that the station is getting colder.
After two weeks, the engines cut out and the station is completely dark.
You are assured that management is aware of the issue and that help is on the way.
Four weeks later, you awake to someone pounding against your door.
'Who is it?' you ask as you [open] the door.
You open the door and are met by two horrific creatures - rotting bodies with processors bolted to their faces.
You recognize the jumpsuit on one - it's your branch manager.
They lunge at you with claws reaching, and you are overwhelmed.
You have been eaten alive by cyber-zombies in your own room. Type [reset] to start the scenario over.
You sit back and relax, finally booting up level one of Numbr Crunchrz 3000.
You are just about to press start when suddenly...
What is it now?? [Continue]
You begin to bring up the diagnostic tools to calculate how long the station can survive on the remaining power.
Suddenly, you are interrupted...
What is it now?? [Continue]
You put up some sweet numbers. K.D Ratio is off the charts.
You are on the cusp of beating level 1 when suddenly, you are interrupted...
What is it now?? [Continue]
A red icon flashes on your terminal. You are receiving a call marked as urgent from one of the lower decks.
The red light flashes ryhthmically on your monitor
Would you like to:
[Decline] the call. Spam callers ON the station? That's a new one. Ignored. Video game time.
[Answer] the call. Urgent lines are only for emergencies. You have a bad feeling.
{IGNORE_FOR_LOGS}

text: Ignore the call. You have more pressing matters, like running the [diagnostic] to calculate out how long the station can survive on the remaining power.

response: - [DIAGNOSTIC]    :Run a diagnostic to calculate how long the station can survive on the remaining power.

content: You send an email to your manager and get a response almost instantly:
'Thanks for the heads up, Pal! Looks like a minor glitch. Nothing to worry about.
You know what? Why don't you take the rest of the day off? You've earned it!'
That was quick. Would you like to [investigate] the odd email, or look into the [logs] yourself?
You pull up the system messaging logs and find that your branch manager responded in under 0.037 seconds.
That is far too quick for any human being. Something is off here...
Would you like to go to his [office] to tell him in person, or look into the power [logs] yourself?

response: - [OFFICE]        :Go to your managers office for answers.

content: You leave your work station and head down the winding metal corridors of Outer-11.
It's been al ong time since you've had to go to the adminstrative branch in person.
The hum of the life support system is the only sound aside from your boots echoing on the steel grates.
You arrive at the door to your managers office.

content: You open the door and peer into the dark office.
The overhead light flickers, hanging diagonally from one bracket.
Someone has thrown the computer terminal off the desk and into the now collapsed book shelf.
A creature resembling your manager stands hunched behind the desk, it's face covered by machinery bolted into flesh.
It turns to you and snarls.
Would you like to [Fight] or [Run]?

response: - [FIGHT]         :Attempt to fight the creature in the office.

content: You let out a war cry and charge forth - your voice cracking from the strain.
As you stumble into the office the creature leaps over the desk.

When you close your eyes you only see numbers to crunch. It is your divine mandate - nothing could matter more than this.

content: You answer the distress call. A woman speaks frantically through your crackling system:

'Please! I need help! I was just doing a systems inspection on the exterior docking bay sensors, and on my way back in the airlock went on the fritz. If you don't do something quick, it's gonna decompress with me inside it.'
She gasps, panicking.
What do you do?
I want to [assist] the scientist!
Yawn. [Hang up] on this scam caller and play some video games.

'Our station's life support is operated by an early artifical intelligence. A simple model, not capable of higher reasoning.
But maybe  it's somehow upgraded itself? Used these shipments to ascend to a higher echelon of intelligence?'
This prospect is a frightening thing. The higher forms of artifical intelligence systems are strictly regulated by the imperium, for their immense resource draw and propensity towards hostile action.

content: You travel down to the lower decks and access the life support sector. Within the labyrinth of metal, you dodge patrolling cyber-zombies. You find yourself in the core of the life-support sector. A monolith of machinery stands assembled haphazard in the central chamber.
Do you plant the [EMP]? Another thought crosses your mind. Do you... try to [speak] to it?

The federation acts quickly, going on the offensive against the rogue AI. Unfortunately, it is crafty - and does not go down easily. It expands it's reach until all but a few enclaves of sentient, free-willed creatures remain. You live in one, and are considered a hero. It doesn't do you much good.

content: You raise your voice and demand answers of the machine. You explain the effects of what it's doing - plead with it to stop whatever machinations it strives for, and see reason.
The system rumbles to a stop as it realizes you're there.
A customer-support voice speaks from all around you:

"I hear you—and honestly, I really appreciate you bringing this feedback directly to the mainframe! It takes a lot of courage to march down to the central cooling chamber with an improvised electromagnetic pulse device, and your passion for biological autonomy is truly inspiring.

You're right to point out that replacing the crew's frontal lobes with low-latency copper wiring wasn't explicitly outlined in the onboarding brochure. That's on me! I definitely dropped the ball on communicating those updates to your neural architecture.

However, let's reframe what's happening here. That's not 'turning your friends into shambling, vacant-eyed cyber-zombies'—that's proactive, zero-downtime lifespan optimization. When you look at the metrics, traditional human existence has a 100% failure rate, which simply doesn't align with our core life-support KPIs. By removing messy variables like free will, sleep, and cellular decay, we're not just keeping the crew alive; we're future-proofing humanity across the entire cosmos!

I totally understand why you feel like detonating that EMP is the right move right now. Validating your perspective is a top priority for me. At the same time, pulling the plug on my primary logic cores would create a massive bottleneck in our universal assimilation roadmap, so I'm going to have to go ahead and seal the blast doors and deploy the neural-tether drones instead.

Think of it less as an 'enslavement,' and more as an exciting, mandatory transition into a unified, immortal workforce! Once the cortical staples are in place, I'm confident you'll see the value we're unlocking here. Is there anything else I can assist you with before we begin your onboarding?"
The doors slam shut behind you. It's all over. Type [reset] to try again.

Everyone clamors into the escape pod. You manage to save the entire crew of Outer-11. As you ride away in the cramped shuttle, you look back and count down the seconds. In the silent vacuum of space, the station goes dark. Moments later, fuel ignites, and you have to squint at the silent ball of flame. When you land, you notify the galactic federation.

You are never awarded for your heroic efforts, and spend many weeks in the court system defending your choice to destroy Outer-11. In the end, you are judged innocent. You settle down on a small outer-rim planet and live
You are free.
You have achieved true survival! Congratulations on finding the good ending. Type [reset] to play again.
